neighbours.label: the preposition or verb marking a path's starting point after 'begin/start/originate' ('begins at', 'starting from', 'begins with', 'originate')
fire: The hiking trail begins at the old mill and climbs to the ridge.
The parade route starts at the town hall and ends by the harbor.
Counting starting from the left, the third seat is yours.
The nerve begins at the base of the skull and runs down the neck.
The river originates in the mountains far to the north.
The ceremony begins with a short prayer by the elder.
The railway line starts from the capital and heads east.
The tour begins at the main gate every hour on the hour.
quiet: The hiking trail passes the old mill on the way to the ridge.
The parade route is lined with flags along the harbor.
Counting the seats on the left, there are twelve in all.
The nerve lies close to the skin along the neck.
The river is wide and slow in the farmland to the north.
The ceremony was long and the elder spoke for an hour.
The railway line is busy and the trains run east.
The tour is popular and the main gate is crowded.
